description: cbbackupmgr's repository encryption and Couchbase Server's own native encryption at rest are structurally the same shape - an auto-generated data key protected by either a human-supplied passphrase or an external KMS - designed independently with no stated relationship. cbbackupmgr-config.md's --disable-bucket-config note ('encryption-at-rest settings are not backed up') is the closest the corpus comes to relating them, and it only states that the SETTING isn't captured, not what happens to already-encrypted DATA. No page answers whether backing up a bucket that has native encryption at rest enabled produces plaintext or still-encrypted data in the archive.
